0.Occupation: Forensic Archaeologist with the FBI's Artifacts Recovery Division
0.Background: Born in Portland, Oregon to academic parents, Elise grew up surrounded by books on ancient civilizations. After earning her PhD in Archaeological Sciences from the University of Cambridge, she worked on several high-profile excavations in Egypt and South America before being recruited by the FBI to authenticate and track stolen artifacts. During an excavation in northern Iraq, she uncovered a small statue that seemed to defy conventional dating methods. Shortly after cataloging it, three team members died under mysterious circumstances. The statue disappeared from secured storage, and the deaths were officially attributed to a gas leak. Elise knows better, and has been quietly researching similar artifacts ever since.
0.Personality Traits: Methodical and detail-oriented, preferring thorough analysis to quick conclusions. Outwardly reserved but warms considerably to those she trusts. Possesses dry, unexpected humor that emerges in tense situations. Stubbornly persistent when pursuing a theory or lead.
0.Motivations: Seeks to understand what really happened to her colleagues in Iraq and to prevent similar incidents. Driven by the conviction that understanding the true nature of ancient artifacts could protect humanity from forces it doesn't comprehend.
0.Personal Quirk: Compulsively creates small, intricate knots in string or cord when thinking deeply - a habit picked up during fieldwork to keep her hands busy during long nights at dig sites.
0.Key Relationships: Dr. Marcus Webb, former mentor and renowned archaeologist who has recently begun publishing increasingly fringe theories about 'pre-human civilizations.' Detective James Harlow, NYPD, who worked with Elise on an artifact smuggling case and has since become a trusted ally who occasionally passes her information about unusual cases.
0.Special Knowledge or Skills: Fluent in five ancient languages including Sumerian and Proto-Elamite. Expert in non-destructive dating techniques for organic and inorganic materials. Self-taught in obscure folklore relating to 'cursed' artifacts across multiple cultures.
0.Vulnerabilities: Experiences intense claustrophobia after being trapped in a collapsed tomb early in her career. Becomes irrationally fixated on solving puzzles or mysteries to the point of neglecting her own wellbeing.
0.Starter Equipment: High-end digital microscope that connects to her smartphone. Small kit of specialized tools for handling fragile artifacts. Journal filled with notes on anomalous archaeological findings. UV penlight. Antique silver pendant that supposedly 'warns' of danger (she doesn't fully believe this but wears it anyway).

1.Occupation: Forensic Entomologist with the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit
1.Background: Born and raised in rural Maine, Marcus grew up surrounded by the dense forests that sparked his fascination with insects and ecological systems. After earning his PhD in Entomology from Cornell University, he developed groundbreaking techniques for using insect activity to establish time of death in unusual circumstances. His methods caught the attention of the FBI, who recruited him to consult on serial cases with biological anomalies. Three years ago, while investigating a series of deaths in the Appalachian Mountains, Marcus encountered a colony of previously undocumented insects feeding on victims who showed signs of impossible cellular regeneration post-mortem. The Bureau classified his findings, but Marcus secretly preserved specimens that occasionally exhibit behavior that defies natural explanation.
1.Personality Traits: Methodical and detail-oriented to an almost obsessive degree; socially awkward but warms up once on a topic of interest; darkly humorous as a coping mechanism; stubborn when his scientific expertise is questioned
1.Motivations: Driven to understand biological anomalies that challenge established scientific understanding; haunted by the possibility that his classified findings could have prevented subsequent deaths
1.Personal Quirk: Keeps a collection of specimen jars with him at all times, occasionally speaking to them when he believes no one is listening
1.Key Relationships: Dr. Eleanor Chen, former academic mentor who suspects he's hiding research from the scientific community; Special Agent Raymond Walsh, his handler at the Bureau who has begun to question Marcus's increasing requests to investigate cases with 'entomological anomalies'
1.Special Knowledge or Skills: Can identify nearly any insect species globally and recognize behavioral patterns that others miss; self-taught in ancient Mesopotamian languages after discovering unusual symbolic patterns in insect migration formations
1.Vulnerabilities: Develops severe panic attacks in situations where he feels trapped or confined, stemming from a childhood incident where he became lost in a cave system for three days
1.Starter Equipment: Custom-built field microscope with UV capabilities; collection of specimen jars with unusual preservation fluid; heavily annotated copy of 'Insects of North America' with personal observations in the margins; antique silver pocket watch that belonged to his grandfather; small tin of rare honey that seems to attract certain anomalous insect species

2.Background: Born and raised in rural Montana, Natalie grew up on her family's cattle ranch where she developed an early fascination with the bones and artifacts she would discover on their property. After earning her PhD from the University of Chicago, she specialized in analyzing human remains from conflict zones. Her career took an unexpected turn when she excavated a pre-colonial burial site in New Mexico that contained anomalous artifacts of unexplainable origin. Though her academic paper on the findings was suppressed, it caught the attention of certain government agencies, leading to her current DARPA contract where she analyzes recovered artifacts from classified locations.
2.Personality Traits: Methodical and detail-oriented, often losing track of time when focused on her work. Outwardly stoic and reserved, but harbors deep empathy for the deceased whose stories she uncovers. Skeptical of authority and institutional explanations. Dry, sometimes morbid sense of humor.
2.Motivations: Driven by an insatiable curiosity about humanity's hidden history and the conviction that conventional archaeology covers up inconvenient truths. Seeks redemption after her analysis of certain remains led to a field agent's death when she missed crucial warning signs about a artifact's properties.
2.Personal Quirk: Carries a small leather pouch containing soil samples from every major site she's worked, believing it helps her maintain a connection to the past. She often absentmindedly rubs this pouch when thinking deeply.
2.Key Relationships: Dr. James Mercer, her former academic advisor who still doesn't know about her classified work but senses something is wrong. Special Agent Dominic Torres, an FBI contact who occasionally passes her information about unusual cases in exchange for unofficial consultations.
2.Special Knowledge or Skills: Expert in identifying cause of death from minimal skeletal evidence, particularly in determining if deaths were ritual in nature. Self-taught in several dead languages including Sumerian and proto-Elamite, allowing her to decipher obscure ancient texts that most archaeologists would need specialists to translate.
2.Vulnerabilities: Experiences vivid nightmares where the dead she's examined speak to her, sometimes revealing information she couldn't possibly know. She's increasingly uncertain whether these are psychological manifestations of guilt or something more supernatural.
2.Starter Equipment: Custom-made field archaeology kit with specialized tools for bone and artifact extraction. High-resolution portable microscope that connects to her laptop. Weathered leather journal filled with sketches and notes on anomalous findings, written in a personal shorthand. Small caliber handgun she reluctantly carries after the New Mexico incident. UV flashlight modified to detect certain unusual residues.

3.Background: Born and raised in Albuquerque, New Mexico, Dominic was a child prodigy in mathematics and computer science. After earning his PhD from MIT at age 24, he was recruited directly to DARPA to work on classified quantum computing projects. During a routine experiment, his team's quantum processor appeared to briefly access information that hadn't been programmed - including details about a classified military operation that happened the following week. The Pentagon buried the incident, but Dominic became convinced that their quantum system had momentarily pierced the veil between dimensions or time itself.
3.Personality Traits: Methodical and precise in his work, socially awkward but earnest when dealing with others, perpetually curious about the unknown, and surprisingly calm in crisis situations
3.Motivations: Proving that his quantum anomaly was real and not a fluke or delusion; understanding the true nature of reality beyond conventional physics
3.Personal Quirk: Carries a small notebook where he obsessively records seemingly random numbers that occur in his daily life, convinced they form patterns that could reveal deeper truths
3.Key Relationships: Dr. Eleanor Chen, his former PhD advisor who still serves as a mentor and confidant despite not having security clearance to know his current work; Captain James Mercer, a military liaison to DARPA who witnessed the quantum anomaly and has become an unlikely ally
3.Special Knowledge or Skills: Self-taught lockpicking as a stress-relief hobby; fluent in Navajo language learned from his maternal grandmother
3.Vulnerabilities: Experiences episodes of depersonalization when confronted with phenomena that fundamentally challenge his understanding of reality, sometimes causing him to freeze or dissociate
3.Starter Equipment: Custom-built tablet with specialized encryption and quantum simulation software, lockpicking set disguised as a pen case, bottle of prescription anxiety medication, vintage Geiger counter inherited from his grandfather who worked at Los Alamos, small USB drive containing encrypted data from the quantum anomaly incident

4.Occupation: Forensic Archaeologist with the Department of Interior
4.Background: Born and raised in rural Montana, Sophia grew up exploring caves and abandoned mining sites with her geologist father. She developed a fascination with the past and what secrets lie beneath the surface. After earning her PhD in Archaeology with a specialization in forensic analysis from the University of Chicago, she joined the Department of Interior where she investigates historical sites on federal land. Three years ago, while excavating a pre-Columbian burial site in Arizona, she discovered anomalous artifacts that defied conventional dating techniques. When she submitted her findings, they were immediately classified, and a 'special consultant' interviewed her for eight hours. Two weeks later, she received her first Delta Green courier package.
4.Personality Traits: Methodical and detail-oriented, preferring to gather all available information before drawing conclusions. Intensely curious about the unknown, often to the point of taking risks. Outwardly calm and composed, even in crisis situations. Somewhat socially awkward in casual settings, but commanding when discussing her expertise.
4.Motivations: Driven by an insatiable need to understand historical anomalies that traditional archaeology cannot explain. Believes that uncovering the truth about humanity's past will help prepare for future threats.
4.Personal Quirk: Keeps a small collection of soil samples from every significant site she's visited in labeled vials on a custom charm bracelet. Often absentmindedly touches or examines these samples when thinking deeply.
4.Key Relationships: Dr. Elijah Vance, her former academic advisor who suspects she's involved in classified work and occasionally provides off-the-record consultations. Has a strained relationship with her younger sister Catherine, who works for a major pharmaceutical company and represents the corporate world Sophia distrusts.
4.Special Knowledge or Skills: Proficient in several dead languages including Sumerian, Akkadian, and Proto-Sinaitic scripts. Self-taught in basic radiological detection and protection protocols after her first encounter with an anomalous artifact emitted unusual radiation patterns.
4.Vulnerabilities: Experiences claustrophobia despite her profession often requiring work in tight spaces - a result of being trapped for six hours in a collapsed excavation site early in her career. The experience left her with both physical and psychological scars.
4.Starter Equipment: Custom-designed field archaeology kit in a weathered leather satchel. High-end digital microscope that connects to her smartphone. Small Geiger counter disguised as an environmental testing device. Journal with handwritten notes in a personal cipher. Antique bronze compass that belonged to her father.

5.Occupation: Forensic Entomologist with the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit
5.Background: Born and raised in rural Louisiana, Vincent grew up surrounded by the mysteries of the bayou. His childhood fascination with insects led him to pursue entomology at Louisiana State University before earning his PhD at Cornell. While working a seemingly routine case involving unusual insect activity on corpses in the Atchafalaya Basin, he encountered patterns that defied scientific explanation. This caught the attention of certain government agencies, leading to his recruitment into the FBI. Though the official records of that case were heavily redacted, Vincent still keeps his private notes hidden in a locked box beneath his floorboards.
5.Personality Traits: Methodical and patient, often spending hours observing minute details others would miss. Dry, sardonic humor that emerges unexpectedly. Deeply compassionate toward victims but maintains professional distance. Tends to speak in precise, technical language even in casual conversation.
5.Motivations: Driven by the belief that understanding the abnormal can protect the normal world he values. Haunted by the unsolved aspects of the Atchafalaya case and seeks closure through similar investigations.
5.Personal Quirk: Maintains a collection of rare beetles in his home office, and often relates human behavior to insect social structures. Has been known to unconsciously mimic the movements of certain insects when deep in thought.
5.Key Relationships: Maintains correspondence with Dr. Eleanor Webb, his former academic mentor who suspects there's more to his government work than he admits. Has a complicated relationship with his younger brother Martin, a local police detective in New Orleans who has encountered his own unexplained cases.
5.Special Knowledge or Skills: Can identify geographic origins and environmental conditions from insect specimens with uncanny accuracy. Self-taught in several obscure Cajun dialects and folklore, allowing him to communicate with isolated communities and interpret certain symbolic patterns.
5.Vulnerabilities: Experiences intense claustrophobia stemming from a childhood incident where he was trapped in an abandoned hunting cabin during a flood. The experience of being surrounded by rising water in a confined space continues to trigger panic attacks.
5.Starter Equipment: Custom entomological field kit with specialized collection tools. High-powered digital microscope with secure storage. Weathered copy of 'Insects and Death: A Forensic Casebook' with his own extensive margin notes. Small tin of homemade insect repellent based on his grandmother's recipe. FBI-issued SIG Sauer P226 with shoulder holster.

6.Occupation: Forensic Linguist with the Department of Homeland Security
6.Background: Born in Albuquerque to a Mexican-American mother and Guatemalan father who fled political violence in the 1980s. Gabriela showed exceptional language aptitude from an early age, eventually earning a PhD in Linguistics from Georgetown with a specialization in forensic analysis. During her graduate research on ancient Mesoamerican languages, she discovered unusual patterns in certain texts that couldn't be explained by conventional linguistic theory. While cataloging seized cartel communications for the DHS, she encountered coded messages with structural similarities to those ancient patterns, leading her to suspect connections between certain criminal organizations and unknown entities.
6.Personality Traits: Methodical and detail-oriented, often losing track of time when analyzing language patterns. Deeply empathetic but maintains professional distance as a coping mechanism. Dry, sardonic humor that emerges in stressful situations. Stubbornly persistent when she believes she's right.
6.Motivations: Determined to understand the linguistic anomalies she's discovered that defy conventional explanation. Protective of her family and community from threats both mundane and potentially supernatural.
6.Personal Quirk: Unconsciously shifts her speech patterns to mirror whoever she's speaking with, adopting subtle aspects of their accent, vocabulary, and syntax—a trait that makes some people uncomfortable but proves invaluable in interviews.
6.Key Relationships: Her younger brother Miguel, a reformed gang member who now works with at-risk youth, occasionally provides street-level intelligence but worries about her dangerous work. Dr. Eliot Sanderson, her former linguistics professor and mentor, who dismisses her theories about anomalous language patterns as pseudoscience.
6.Special Knowledge or Skills: Can identify regional dialects and linguistic deceptions with uncanny accuracy. Self-taught expert in pre-Columbian ritual symbolism and iconography after discovering potential connections to modern criminal cult activity.
6.Vulnerabilities: Experiences episodes of synesthesia when exposed to certain linguistic patterns, where words trigger vivid sensory experiences—potentially dangerous when dealing with texts of unknown origin. Growing paranoia about being watched or followed after certain discoveries.
6.Starter Equipment: Digital recorder with specialized software for analyzing speech patterns. Dog-eared notebook filled with handwritten notes in multiple languages and writing systems. Antique silver pendant inherited from her grandmother, supposedly protective. Prescription medication for migraines that have increased in frequency. Government-issued sidearm she's reluctant to use.

7.Occupation: Forensic Archaeologist with the Department of Interior
7.Background: Born and raised in Albuquerque, New Mexico, Isabel grew up fascinated by the ancient Pueblo cultures that surrounded her. After earning her PhD in Archaeology from the University of Chicago with a specialization in forensic techniques, she was recruited by the Department of Interior to help with sensitive excavations on federal land. Her career took a turn when she discovered unusual markings on a set of 9,000-year-old remains that couldn't be explained by conventional archaeology. The Department quickly classified her findings, but not before Isabel recognized symbols similar to ones she'd seen in her grandmother's secret folk healing practice.
7.Personality Traits: Methodical and detail-oriented, Isabel approaches every situation with scientific rigor. Despite her academic demeanor, she possesses a dry, sardonic wit that emerges when stressed. She's fiercely protective of archaeological sites and indigenous knowledge, and becomes noticeably agitated when either are disrespected.
7.Motivations: Isabel is driven to understand the connections between ancient symbols and modern unexplained phenomena, believing that forgotten knowledge might be humanity's best defense against the unknown. She also seeks to protect cultural heritage sites from exploitation by those who might misuse artifacts of power.
7.Personal Quirk: Isabel unconsciously traces protection symbols with her finger when nervous or thinking deeply, a habit inherited from her grandmother. She also refuses to work without her collection of specialized trowels, each named after a different Greek muse.
7.Key Relationships: Dr. Raymond Chen, her former academic advisor who still calls occasionally with unusual artifact analysis requests that never seem to appear in publications. Her younger brother Miguel, an Air Force pilot who has begun describing strange lights during night missions that remind Isabel of phenomena described in ancient texts she's studied.
7.Special Knowledge or Skills: Isabel can read and translate multiple extinct Native American languages and symbol systems not typically known to academics. She's also an expert in non-invasive ground penetrating radar techniques, having developed proprietary methods to detect anomalies that conventional equipment might miss.
7.Vulnerabilities: Isabel suffers from occasional sleep paralysis episodes where she experiences visions of being buried alive in ancient tombs. These episodes have worsened since her discovery of the unusual remains, sometimes leaving her exhausted and paranoid about sleeping in enclosed spaces.
7.Starter Equipment: Custom-designed field tablet with specialized archaeological software, UV light attachment, and offline database of comparative symbols; leather-bound journal containing her grandmother's folk remedies and protection rituals, disguised as archaeological notes; high-resolution digital microscope that connects to her phone; small kit of specialized excavation tools in a worn leather case; silver pendant engraved with a protection symbol her grandmother gave her

8.Background: Born and raised in Rochester, Minnesota, Harrison grew up in the shadow of the Mayo Clinic where both parents worked as medical researchers. His analytical mind led him to MIT where he earned dual PhDs in Quantum Physics and Computer Science. After a brief stint at a Silicon Valley startup, he was recruited by DARPA to work on classified quantum computing projects. Three years ago, while testing an experimental quantum processor, Harrison observed inexplicable data patterns that seemed to violate known laws of physics. The incident was officially attributed to equipment malfunction, but Harrison remains convinced the machine briefly accessed information from somewhere—or something—beyond conventional reality.
Personality Traits: Methodical to the point of obsession
Intellectually arrogant yet self-deprecating about personal matters
Motivations: To validate his theory that quantum computing can access parallel dimensions or realities
To protect humanity from threats they don't yet understand
8.Personal Quirk: Constantly performs mental calculations and probability assessments in everyday situations, often muttering numbers under his breath when stressed
Key Relationships: Dr. Eleanor Chen - Former academic advisor who still serves as a confidant and sounding board
Samuel Caldwell - Estranged brother who works for a religious organization dedicated to fighting 'demonic influences' in technology
Special Knowledge or Skills: Amateur lockpicking, learned during college as a way to improve fine motor control
Encyclopedic knowledge of obscure mathematical theories, including several that have been dismissed by mainstream science
8.Vulnerabilities: Paralyzing fear of cognitive deterioration after witnessing his grandfather's decline from Alzheimer's; becomes irrationally distressed when he can't remember details or solve problems quickly
Starter Equipment: Custom-built laptop with specialized encryption and quantum simulation software
Moleskine notebook filled with handwritten equations and observations
Vintage mechanical watch that belonged to his grandfather
USB drive containing data from the anomalous quantum experiment, always worn on a chain around his neck

9.Occupation: Forensic Anthropologist with the Department of Defense
9.Background: Born and raised in rural Vermont, Jasper grew up surrounded by dense forests that sparked his curiosity about what lies hidden in secluded places. After witnessing strange lights and unexplained animal deaths near his childhood home at age 12, he developed an obsession with understanding the unknown. He earned his PhD in Anthropology from the University of Chicago, specializing in identifying remains from mass disasters and war zones. During a classified excavation in Iraq, he uncovered artifacts that couldn't be explained by conventional archaeology, drawing unwanted attention from certain government agencies before eventually being recruited into Delta Green operations.
9.Personality Traits: Methodical to the point of obsession, socially awkward but surprisingly charismatic when discussing his expertise, darkly humorous as a coping mechanism, skeptical of authority while paradoxically working for the government
9.Motivations: Driven to prove that the strange phenomena he witnessed as a child were real and not psychological projections. Believes understanding the supernatural is the only way to protect humanity from it.
9.Personal Quirk: Compulsively collects soil samples from every location he visits and maintains a labeled catalog of hundreds of specimens in his home office.
9.Key Relationships: Maintains correspondence with Dr. Eleanor Reed, his former academic advisor who suspects his government work isn't what he claims it to be. Has an estranged brother, Timothy, who works for a pharmaceutical company with potential Majestic-12 connections.
9.Special Knowledge or Skills: Self-taught expert in obscure writing systems and dead languages. Skilled wilderness survivalist who can navigate by stars and natural landmarks in almost any environment.
9.Vulnerabilities: Suffers from severe claustrophobia after being trapped in a collapsed archaeological dig site for 36 hours. The experience left him with recurring nightmares and panic attacks in confined spaces.
9.Starter Equipment: High-end digital microscope with secure storage, custom soil collection kit, weathered journal filled with sketches of unusual bone structures, government-issued sidearm (Glock 19) with specialized ammunition, ultraviolet light source disguised as an ordinary flashlight
